entries.german:
Die Gebrüder Rudolf und Rudolf Grafen von Wert heim kaufen vom Fuldaer Abt Heinrich das Dorf Cellingen. 1327. März 16.

Nos Henricus dei gratia Fuldensis ecclcsie Abbas. Ad universorum tam presentium quam futurorum deducimus no- titiam publice in bis scriptis, quod honorabilibus ac nobilibus viris Rudolfo de Wertheim, canonico majoris ecclesie Herbip., et Rudolfo Comiti de Wertheim fratribus pro se et suis he- redibus ementibus et recipientibus villam nostram Oellingen cum omnibus pertinentiis nobis et nostre ecclesie in ipsa villa competentibus, quesitis et inquirendis, herbergis nostris duntaxat exceptis, quas nobis et nostris successoribus reser vantes, de consensu unanimi, voluntario et expresso dilec- torum in Christo filiorum Theodorici decani totiusque con- ventus ecclesie mee pref. maturo consilio, solemnique trac- tatu cum eisdem super hoc diligentius prehabitis, vendidimus et tradidimus pro pretio quingentarum libr. hall. nobis pre- dictos emptores in parata et numerata pecunia soluto ac in evidentes nostras et ecclesie nostre utilitates exposito et converso nee non justo venditionis titulo damus et Iradimus libere per presentes, hoc tamen moderaminc addito, quod nobis et successoribus nostris ex specialis favoris ipsorum emptorum indultu predict. villam cum juribus suis et perti nentiis, ut prescribitur, apud diet. Rudolfum canonicum prin- cipaliter, si pro tempore vixerit, ac ipso nоn existente apud prelib. Rudolfum Comitem ipsius fratrem vel suos heredes pro antedicto pretio D libr. hall. dativorum anno quocunque voluerint reemendi libera sit facultas, dummodo XIV diebus festum cathedre s. Petri precedentibus immediate aut sequen- tibus per nos reemptio ipsa fiat, qua reemptione sic facta dicta villa cum omnibus juribus et pertinentiis, quibus nobis pertinere noscebat, ad nos et nostram eccl. sine impedimento quolibet libere revolvetur nee ipsam villam a persona seu personis quavis alia vel aliis quam per nos ipsos et nostram eccles. reemi ullatenus admittemus. [Es folgen dann die ge wöhnlichen Cautionsformeln des römischen Rechts in Kauf briefen] — In cujus rei testimonium et memoriam firmiorem nostr. et conventus nostri Fuld. sigilla presentibus sunt ap- pensa. Nos quoque Theodoricus decan. et convent. pred. ex certa nostra scientia recognoseimus nostrum sigill. etiam appendisse. entries.english:
The brothers Rudolf and Rudolf, Counts of Wertheim, purchase the village of Cellingen from Abbot Heinrich of Fulda. 16 March 1327.

“Henry, by the grace of God Abbot of the Church of Fulda,” makes known to all present and future that, with the unanimous, voluntary, and express consent of his beloved sons in Christ, Dean Theodoric and the entire chapter of his church, after due deliberation and careful discussion, he has sold and conveyed to the honorable and noble men Rudolf of Wertheim, canon of Würzburg’s principal church, and Rudolf, Count of Wertheim, brothers, for themselves and their heirs, the abbey’s village of Oellingen with all appurtenances belonging to him and his church there, whether known or yet to be discovered. The abbey’s lodgings are excepted and reserved for him and his successors. The price of 500 pounds of Hall silver has been paid in ready cash and applied to the manifest advantage of the abbot and his church; by this deed he freely grants and conveys the village by lawful sale. A condition is added: by special favor granted to the buyers, the abbot and his successors may redeem the village, with its rights and appurtenances, for the stated price of 500 pounds of Hall pennies in whatever year they wish, first from Rudolf the canon if he is then living, and otherwise from Rudolf the Count or his heirs. The redemption must be made within the fourteen days immediately before or after the Feast of the Chair of St Peter. Upon redemption, the village and all rights and appurtenances that had belonged to the abbot and his church will return freely and without hindrance to them; no person other than the abbot and his church may redeem it. The customary Roman-law security clauses in deeds of sale follow. The seals of the abbot and his convent, and also the dean and convent’s seal, are attached. Done and issued in the year of the Lord 1327, on the Monday after the Sunday on which Oculi is sung.
